Independent spectral spacing and coordinate slice calculation
correctness.rationale: With the period-one Fourier basis, the eigenvalue of −Δ is 4π²N for integer N=k₁²+k₂². Parseval gives η=r_h²/(4π²h²)² as the sum of shell masses times squared distance to R²=1/(4π²h²). Choose a nearest integer N*, including the possibility of a tie. All other integer shells are at distance at least 1/2, so the complementary squared norm is at most 4η=o(1); for small h the selected shell must be populated, since otherwise this bound would contradict normalization. For v on that shell, Parseval in x₁ at each x₂ leaves one sum for each k₁, with at most two terms (k₂ solving k₂²=N*−k₁²). Cauchy–Schwarz bounds the x₁-integrated density by 2||v||² everywhere, and the x₂ measure of the tube is 2√h. Thus M(v)≤4√h||v||² and M(u_h)≤8√h||v||²+2||u_h−v||²→0. The bounds do not presume any Diophantine support or any particular rate within o(h²), and imply the 7/8 limsup corollary.
residual_risks: The referenced DRAFT.md was not present in the frozen package; the effective proof is contained in RESULT.md.
No implication is certified for general perturbations or arbitrary O(h) residuals; the stated conditional theorem does not guarantee existence at every h.

evidence: Zygmund's uniform L⁴ implies ∫_E |v|²≤C²|E|^(1/2)||v||² for any measurable E and any square-torus eigenfunction, and thus stronger geometric coverage for the vanishing limit.
Blair–Sogge relate subcritical L⁴ growth and power savings in λ^(−1/2) tubes on surfaces for exact eigenfunctions; λ is comparable to h^(−1) here.

Bourgain–Rudnick discuss the distinct arbitrary segment restriction problem and give an almost-all-energy result; neither is needed for the complete horizontal slice. Perturbed quasimodes in Macià–Rivière use different scales and operators.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Transfer the applicable eigenfunction estimate by the elementary gap argument; do not equate general restriction at all energies or wider perturbed quasimodes with the frozen hypotheses.

evidence: The precise deduction is ||1_{E_h}u_h||₂≤C|E_h|^(1/4)||v_h||₂+2√η, with η defined by the exact residual and spacing. It tends to zero for every |E_h|→0.

This does not give the numerical constant 4 for the shell estimate; that constant comes directly from the full horizontal Fourier slice: each horizontal frequency has at most two perpendicular frequencies, and the slice family has width 2√h.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The stronger geometric vanishing conclusion follows from already known uniform integrability plus an exact spectral projection, not from a conjectural lattice estimate. The sharper shell constant is a one-step consequence of coordinate Parseval and a quadratic equation, not new control of quasimode scarring.

evidence: The square-torus uniform L⁴ estimate for exact eigenfunctions is stated in Macià–Rivière with a citation to Zygmund.

Under the exact residual and normalization in the frozen claim, projection on a single shell changes the function by o(1) in L². On any measurable E_h, truncated L² norms differ by at most this distance.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Below the h² spacing the frozen qualitative assertion is equivalent to its exact-eigenfunction version, along the allowed sequences of h and with tube widths comparable to those at the exact shell energy. The use of quasimodes does not create a genuinely distinct concentration regime for this conclusion.

originality.rationale: The qualitative no-concentration result for the exact residual regime is an immediate corollary of the classical uniform square-torus eigenfunction L⁴ bound and projection across the constant integer-shell spacing, and holds in any measurable sets of shrinking area. The additional O(√h) estimate on the projected eigenfunction is simply the elementary multiplicity-two coordinate restriction estimate integrated over the width. The exact named match is the same record, not independent prior evidence.
residual_risks: The original Zygmund full text was not inspected. The affirmative implication uses an inspected published statement of the uniform bound.
No claim is made about first publication of the exact constant or about arbitrary wider window estimates.

checked_sources: Uniform L⁴ comparison and independent horizontal slice estimate
value.rationale: The residual is smaller than one spectral-shell gap, so the motivating scarring threshold is already excluded by elementary projection and classical uniform integrability. For the exact horizontal tube the added shell bound is a direct coordinate orthogonality exercise, and the tail term gives no independent rate of decay for arbitrary o(h²) residuals. The record does not resolve a wider spectral window or geometrically nontrivial concentration mechanism. The stated case is a useful illustration, not new substantive evidence about scarring.
residual_risks: A quantitatively motivated estimate for truly wider windows or perturbed operators would be a separate question.
